newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Foreign buying supports Pibor volatility.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Foreign buying supports Pibor volatility.

text.p: Buying by foreign investors of Pibor options pushed volatility slightly higher on Monday, reversing a decline at the start of the session, traders said.
Political polls released over the weekend suggested the centre-right government's lead over the left in the election campaign was widening. Polls last week showed the left gaining ground.

"Although volatility is expensive, there is still sufficient chance for the Socialists to get in to keep it high," said a broker at a French brokerage in Paris. "There is also a large risk-premium about monetary union priced in."

The IFOP poll for the weekly Journal Dimanche, conducted on Friday, gave the centre-right 41 percent of the vote, up three points from a similar poll last week, and 38.5 percent for the combined left, a 2.5 percent dip from the previous week. The election is due to be held on May 25 and June 1.

Traders said investors saw a Socialist government as less willing to pursue stringent austerity measures, if France appears likely to miss the Maastrich criteria necessary to participate in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
Even if the current government were re-elected, the path towards meeting the criteria was still expected to be difficult, particularly with unemployment running at just under 13 percent.
"After the election, volatility will come off, but it won't collapse," said Ian Aubrey, head of futures and options sales at Yamaichi International in London.

June Pibor volatility was at 35-36 percent, up from 35 percent at the open, but little changed from Friday. The 96.40 strike, one of the most active so far this session, traded at a volatility of 36.1 percent. A buyer bought 1,500 straddles at that strike.
September options were trading at 21-23 percent, down from 24 percent on Friday, and December was at 20-20.5 percent, down around 50 basis points.
June Pibor futures were up seven basis points at 96.41 by 1100 GMT. September futures were up 0.05 at 96.48.
June notionnel volatility rose to 3.9-4.0 percent, compared with 3.8 percent on Friday.
June notionnel futures were up 0.24 at 129.98. Traders said call activity dominated the options market. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
